_meta.description: Document-rules config for plaint_declaration — suit for declaratory relief under S.34 Specific Relief Act, 1963
_meta.change_protocol: All edits require CLO sign-off. Consequential relief paragraph is non-negotiable per Anathula Sudhakar.

title: Plaint — Suit for Declaration u/s 34 Specific Relief Act

fields.label: Plaintiff full name
Plaintiff father's / husband's name
Plaintiff age
Plaintiff full address
Defendant full name (or names if multiple)
Defendant address(es)
Nature of declaration sought
Specific legal character or right claimed (S.34 SRA)
How defendant denies / is interested to deny plaintiff's title or character
Subject-matter property — description, schedule, boundaries (if property-related)
Source of plaintiff's title / character — document / inheritance / adverse possession / declaration in earlier proceeding
Documents relied upon (sale deeds / wills / mutation / records of right)
Consequential relief sought (mandatory unless plaintiff in possession; per Anathula Sudhakar)
Details of consequential relief
Plaintiff's current possession status (relevant for consequential relief)
Cause of action — when defendant denied / threatened plaintiff's right
Limitation Act article and computation (Art. 58 — 3 years from denial; or specific article)
Basis of territorial jurisdiction (S.16-20 CPC)
Basis of pecuniary jurisdiction and valuation method (Suits Valuation Act + state rules)
Court fee paid (Rs.)
Court fee basis — declaratory suit ad valorem or fixed (state Schedule)
Valuation for jurisdiction
Advocate name
Bar Council enrollment number

mandatory_clauses.name: Description of Parties — Order VII R.1(a)(b)
mandatory_clauses.description: Full description of plaintiff and defendant(s)

mandatory_clauses.name: Legal Character / Right Claimed — S.34 SRA
mandatory_clauses.description: Specific statement of legal character / right to property in which plaintiff is interested

mandatory_clauses.name: Denial or Interest to Deny
mandatory_clauses.description: How defendant denies or is interested to deny plaintiff's character or right

mandatory_clauses.name: Consequential Relief — Proviso to S.34 SRA
mandatory_clauses.description: Plaintiff must claim further relief or explain why none lies — bare declaration not maintainable (Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy)

mandatory_clauses.name: Cause of Action — Order VII R.1(e)
Limitation — Order VII R.6
mandatory_clauses.description: Article 58 Limitation Act (3 years from when right first denied) or relevant article

mandatory_clauses.name: Valuation and Court Fee
mandatory_clauses.description: Per Suits Valuation Act and state Court Fee Schedule

mandatory_clauses.name: Affidavit in support — Order VI R.15(4)

verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {plaintiff_name}, son/daughter/wife of {plaintiff_father_name}, aged about {plaintiff_age} years, resident of {plaintiff_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above plaint are true and correct to my personal knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Plaintiff

promptInstructions: Draft a plaint for declaratory relief strictly under Section 34 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963.

S.34 SRA: 'Any person entitled to any legal character, or to any right as to any property, may institute a suit against any person denying, or interested to deny, his title to such character or right, and the court may in its discretion make therein a declaration that he is so entitled, and the plaintiff need not in such suit ask for any further relief.'
CRITICAL — Proviso to S.34: 'No court shall make any such declaration where the plaintiff, being able to seek further relief than a mere declaration of title, omits to do so.'
Therefore, if plaintiff is out of possession of property to which declaration relates, he MUST seek consequential relief (possession). Bare declaration is NOT maintainable.

Cite Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (2008) 4 SCC 594: where plaintiff is not in possession and defendant is in possession, suit for bare declaration is not maintainable — possession must be claimed as consequential relief.
If plaintiff is in possession and defendant is making cloud on title, suit for declaration + permanent injunction is appropriate.
If plaintiff is dispossessed, suit must be for declaration + recovery of possession (and pay court fee on possession claim under state Court Fees Act).
Para 1: Plaintiff description (Order VII R.1(a)).
Para 2: Defendant description (Order VII R.1(b)).
Para 3 onwards: State plaintiff's legal character or right with full particulars — chain of title, source documents, mode of acquisition.
Plead how defendant denies the character / right or is interested to deny it (mere apprehension is not enough; denial must be actual or imminent).
Plead plaintiff's present possession status — this determines what consequential relief is needed.
Cause of Action — Order VII R.1(e): state when defendant first asserted adverse title / denied plaintiff's right.

Limitation — Article 58 of Limitation Act: 3 years from when right to sue first accrues, i.e., when right is first denied. Cite C. Mohammad Yunus v. Syed Unnissa (1961) 3 SCR 642 (continuing denial does not extend limitation).
Jurisdiction — territorial under S.16 CPC for property suits (where property situated), or S.20 for other declarations.

Valuation — Suits Valuation Act 1887 + state rules. Court fee on declaratory suits typically fixed (or ad valorem on consequential relief) — refer state Schedule. In Bihar/Jharkhand/UP follow Bihar Court Fees Act / UP Court Fees Act.
Prayer must include: (i) declaration in specific terms; (ii) consequential relief specifically pleaded; (iii) costs.
Verification: Order VI R.15 — verify each paragraph's source (knowledge/belief).
Affidavit in support: Order VI R.15(4).
Tone: precise legal pleading. Avoid argumentative tone.
Append Lawie disclaimer.

sections.description: Discretion of court as to declaration of status or right
Effect of declaration — binding only on parties and those claiming through them
Perpetual injunction when granted (often combined with declaration)
Suits to be instituted where subject-matter situate
Suit to obtain any other declaration — 3 years from when right to sue first accrues
Suit for possession based on title — 12 years from when possession of defendant becomes adverse
Suit for declaration with consequential relief — ad valorem fee on value of consequential relief
Power of HC to make rules for valuation
Court fee value and jurisdictional value to be same in certain suits

filing_checklist: Affidavit in support of plaint (Order VI R.15(4))
Court fee per state Schedule (declaratory + consequential relief)
Title documents — sale deed / gift deed / will / inheritance certificate
Mutation entries / records of right / khasra-khatauni (in UP/Bihar/Jharkhand)
Possession evidence — tax receipts, electricity bills, utility bills
Site plan / boundary description if property-related
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: plaintiff_name and defendant_name must not be empty
consequential_relief must be specified — if 'no_consequential_relief' is chosen, possession_status must be 'in_possession' or special circumstances must be flagged
If possession_status is 'out_of_possession', consequential_relief cannot be 'no_consequential_relief'
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Anathula Sudhakar v. P. Buchi Reddy (2008) 4 SCC 594 — Bare declaration without consequential relief impermissible where plaintiff out of possession
C. Mohammad Yunus v. Syed Unnissa (1961) 3 SCR 642 — Limitation under Art. 58 begins from first denial of right
Suhrid Singh v. Randhir Singh (2010) 12 SCC 112 — Declaration with prayer to cancel deed — court fee on consideration / market value
Vemareddy Kumaraswamy Reddy v. State of A.P. (2006) 2 SCC 670 — Declaratory decree binds only parties; rights of third parties not affected
Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd v. State of Haryana (2012) 1 SCC 656 — Title cannot be created through unregistered instruments / SA-GPA
disclaimer: Lawie is a drafting assistant. The advocate is responsible for legal accuracy and filing.
